Problem 1 Structural Chemistry of Aluminosilicates
The fundamental structural unit of silicates is the $[SiO_4]$ tetrahedron. Sharing corner oxygen atoms between silicate tetrahedra can form finite polynuclear anions, one-dimensional chains, two-dimensional layers, and three-dimensional infinite frameworks. Zeolite molecular sieves are aluminosilicates with regular channels and cage structures; their frameworks can be regarded as three-dimensional networks of corner-sharing $[SiO_4]$ and $[AlO_4]$ tetrahedra.

subquestions.text_open: 1.1.4 Describe the long-chain silicate structure with general formula $[Si_4O_{11}]_n^{6n-}$, given that it contains 12-membered rings formed by alternating Si and O atoms.

1.2 Sodalite belongs to the cubic crystal system. In its conventional unit cell, a sodalite cage (β cage) occupies each vertex and the body center, and the cages are connected by sharing hexagonal faces. In addition, each β cage is connected to other β cages by sharing square faces. Each β cage contains four sodium ions arranged as a regular tetrahedron, with a chloride ion at the center of the tetrahedron; each element has only one crystallographically distinct environment.
1.2.4 In the β cage of sodalite, the number of Al atoms is the maximum allowed by Lowenstein's rule. State the lattice type of sodalite.

1.3 In Type A zeolite (LTA), a larger α cage forms at the lattice center. An isolated α cage belongs to the Oh point group and has polyhedral notation [4126886]. The LTA framework may be regarded as a three-dimensional infinite structure in which α cages are connected by sharing regular octagonal faces in a “primitive cubic packing” arrangement. 1.3.1 If each LTA unit cell is regarded as containing 1 α cage, state the number of T atoms in one unit cell of Type A zeolite.

1.4 In the laboratory, 4Å molecular sieve A can be synthesized hydrothermally from sodium silicate, sodium aluminate, and sodium hydroxide.
1.4.3 Write the overall equation for the synthesis of molecular sieve A.
